concept_options.title: Why Perfect Parts Never Fit
concept_options.hook: These parts fit perfectly in CAD. In real life? They're welded.
concept_options.visual_approach: A tactile 2.5D forensic teardown of a pin trapped in a hole. Dark precision-workshop frames alternate with warm drawing-stock diagrams. A thin red clearance gauge appears in the hook at 0.00 and returns only at the payoff when the parts finally move.
concept_options.target_audience: Men 18–34 in India, the US, and Southeast Asia who use CAD, 3D printers, CNC, electronics enclosures, or workshop tools
key_points: CAD dimensions are nominal ideals; every manufacturing process produces a range.
Tolerance describes variation, while clearance is intentional space between mating parts.
The correct fit depends on function and process, so a small fit gauge is more useful than a universal magic number.
concept_options.core_message: Perfect in CAD is not functional in reality; design the fit, then test the process.
concept_options.cta: Episode 2 will show how a fracture line reveals the direction a part was built.
grounded_in: Recurring tolerance-versus-clearance confusion in maker forums
Weak packaging of direct tolerance education on YouTube
Formlabs guidance that fit depends on function, material, and process
concept_options.why_this_works: It attacks a misconception every builder encounters, demonstrates the answer with physical causality, and creates a repeatable series grammar without depending on a presenter.

concept_options.title: The Crack Is a Map
concept_options.hook: That crack is pointing straight at the mistake you made.
concept_options.visual_approach: Open on a suspended broken bracket, then track the fracture path like a crime-scene map through layer direction, stress concentration, and part orientation.
concept_options.target_audience: 3D-printing and fabrication hobbyists troubleshooting structural failures
key_points: Fracture location and direction preserve evidence about loading.
Layer orientation changes strength in anisotropic printed parts.
Geometry can redirect stress away from a weak plane.
concept_options.core_message: A failed part is a free test report if you know how to read it.
concept_options.cta: Next, read the shiny ring around a stripped screw.
grounded_in: Maker appetite for visible failure evidence
concept_options.why_this_works: Failure imagery supplies immediate drama and the forensic framing turns a common frustration into a useful diagnostic habit.

concept_options.title: One Extra Zero
concept_options.hook: One extra zero can multiply a part's cost without improving it.
concept_options.visual_approach: A technical drawing gains decimal places while its production route expands from one tool to multiple slow operations; cost, scrap risk, and inspection stack visually around the dimension.
concept_options.target_audience: Early-career engineers, CAD users, and hardware founders
key_points: A tolerance should be tied to function, not aesthetics on a drawing.
Tighter limits can require slower processes and more inspection.
The widest functional tolerance is often the higher-quality engineering choice.
concept_options.core_message: Precision is a budget you spend only where function demands it.
concept_options.cta: Episode 2 will show the dimension that silently breaks assemblies.
concept_options.why_this_works: It turns an invisible manufacturing rule into a visually escalating cost story with direct relevance to builders who order parts.

concept_options.title: Prototype Is Not Product
concept_options.hook: It worked once. That proves almost nothing about unit one hundred.
concept_options.visual_approach: Follow one handmade prototype as it becomes a row of one hundred units; each manual correction disappears and exposes a repeatability trap.
concept_options.target_audience: Hardware founders and ambitious makers moving toward small-batch production
key_points: A prototype proves concept, not repeatability.
Assembly access, testing, part supply, and process variation appear at batch scale.
Manufacturing constraints should enter before the design freezes.
concept_options.core_message: Design the hundredth unit while you are still building the first.
concept_options.cta: Episode 2 will reveal the test point most founders forget.
concept_options.why_this_works: It targets the most commercially valuable audience pain and uses a clear visual multiplication device, though it is less universal than c1 for a first episode.

concept_options.title: Jugaad That Survives Batch 100
concept_options.hook: This clever shortcut works once. One change makes it repeatable.
concept_options.visual_approach: Split-screen a brilliant one-off fix against a production-minded revision, using the same low-cost materials but adding locating features, strain relief, and testability.
concept_options.target_audience: Resourceful makers and early hardware teams across India and Southeast Asia, with universal relevance for US DIY audiences
key_points: Improvisation is valuable during discovery but must be translated into constraints.
Repeatability comes from locating, fastening, strain relief, and test access.
Production thinking does not require expensive materials; it requires explicit interfaces.
concept_options.core_message: Keep the ingenuity; engineer the repeatability.
concept_options.cta: Episode 2 will test the same fix after heat, dust, and vibration.
grounded_in: Need for low-cost globally adaptable examples
concept_options.why_this_works: It has strong regional texture without excluding the global audience, but requires careful cultural execution, making it better after the channel establishes trust.

selected_concept.rationale: First-ranked and self-approved under the user's unattended-session rule. It is the most universal topic, has the clearest sub-five-second physical hook, and establishes the recurring forensic format and red-gap motif.
modifications: Keep the advice process-specific instead of claiming one universal clearance value.
Use a three-act structure and reserve the red-gap signature device for the hook and payoff only.
Closing line must explicitly tee up the fracture-forensics episode.

stages.approach: Write a 150–175 word, three-act narration with a cold open inside five seconds and performance direction for a calm, credible male voice.
Plan seven visually distinct bespoke scenes with deliberate pacing, title card, recurring red-gap motif, and no repeated primary visual subject.

production_plan.art_direction: projects/faceless-builder-ep1/art-direction.md — Measured Friction: graphite workshop, warm drawing stock, steel cyan, warning red, monospaced measurements, physically motivated motion, and a red clearance-gap signature used only in hook and payoff.

taste_profile.design_read: A precision workshop inside a dark cinema: tactile for makers, exact for engineers, and fast enough for a discovery feed; every motion explains fit, force, or measurement.
taste_profile.palette_discipline: Graphite and warm drawing-stock bases; steel cyan for neutral information, warning red only for interference and clearance, brass only for tools.
taste_profile.layout_variation: Alternate macro evidence, wide title negative space, sectional diagrams, full-frame tolerance fields, mechanical triptych, and tactile test-gauge close-up.
taste_profile.reference_strategy: One generated hook image plus per-scene locally rendered review stills; use Branch/Animagraffs only as clarity references, never as a visual template.
anti_patterns: same hero object in every scene
caption text duplicated as headline text
universal clearance number presented as fact
quality_gates: Cold open resolves visually by second 5.
Each scene has a different primary visual subject.
Signature red gap appears in at most two beats.
Every movement has an explanatory purpose.
Word captions remain readable on mobile-safe center bands.

music_source.mood_direction: 104 BPM restrained mechanical pulse; dry clicks, low synth tension, no vocals, one satisfying release at the Act III fit test.

voice_selection.rationale: Rich male voice with international intelligibility and enough authority for an engineering forensic tone.
voice_selection.delivery_style: Calm expert who enjoys the reveal; precise, never salesy, with a slightly dry edge on the myth flip.
voice_selection.pacing_policy: Fast cold open, 250–350 ms pauses at act turns, slow down for the definitions of tolerance and clearance, then accelerate into the three-fit payoff.
